notes.path: vault/Literature/Papers/Entries/HUMAT- An Integrated Framework for Modelling Individual Motivations- Social Exchange and Network Dynamics.md
notes.source_access: Primary publisher full text and Appendix A accessible at https://www.jasss.org/28/1/4.html.

checks.state: Mostly correct: note names three motive groups, importances, alternative evaluations/satisfactions, aspiration, dissonance tolerance, previous choice/habit, and direct alters. It correctly says chosen alternatives are initially known. It does not specify that the remaining alter-representation entries (motive values/satisfactions, similarities, persuasion values, etc.) default to 0 and become available through communication (Appendix A Table 3 and Sensing, publisher lines 328-363).
checks.schedule: Correct order: at each tick information exchange (Signal/Inquire) precedes attitude formation/Set dissonances; Set dissonances processes agents in random order (Appendix A Process overview and scheduling, lines 364-377, 520). Note gives positive dissonance-strength activation.
checks.signalling_inquiring: Action selection is substantially correct: when dissonance strength >0, both dilemma flags yield equal-probability choice; social-only signals; non-social-only inquires; else no exchange (Appendix A Signal or inquire, lines 477-484). The note omits the definitions that set those flags: social dilemma is social evaluation <0 with at least one other motive evaluation >0; non-social dilemma is social evaluation >=0 with at least one other-motive evaluation <0 (Appendix A Identify dilemmas, lines 533-534).
checks.partner_choice: The stated broad targets are correct: uncontacted, opposite-choice alter prioritized for signaling, uncontacted, same-choice alter for inquiry, then greatest persuasion; signaling uses the alter most gullible to ego and inquiry uses the alter most persuasive to ego (Appendix A Set alter representations, lines 464-473; Signal/Inquire, lines 485-518; narrative lines 407-414). The note omits that contact history is the first sorting key and that if dissonance remains, the next suitable alter is selected at a later time step (lines 413, 473, 502-518).
checks.choice_update: The 10%-of-range staged comparison rule and fallback (random initial choice, otherwise retain habit) are correctly summarized (Appendix A Choose alternative, lines 536-542). The note correctly reports exchange updating evaluations/dissonance/choice, although it simplifies away exact persuasion-weighted equations (Signal/Inquire, lines 486-512).
checks.initialization: Importance and dissonance tolerance Normal(.5,.14), aspiration Uniform[0,1], beta satisfaction, and 20%-of-neighbors-within-35-cells network with nearest-neighbor fallback are represented (Appendix A Initialisation, lines 436-463). The note now explicitly records the source conflict: Stochasticity states aspiration from 0 to <3 (lines 417-423), while Create agents/Table 1 give [0,1] (line 441). It also now flags the narrative/procedure choice-rule conflict: Section 2 says new preference replaces habit only if more satisfying and less dissonant (lines 130-132/376-377), whereas procedural Choose alternative uses satisfaction, then dissonance/experiential satisfaction within 10%-of-range thresholds, and otherwise retains habit (lines 536-542). These conflicts are accurately surfaced. Available beta parameter options (α,β)=(12,4),(8,4),(4,4),(4,8),(4,12) are still omitted (Table 4, lines 453-460).

findings.evidence: Appendix A Identify dilemmas lines 533-534; Table 3 lines 331-363; Set alter representations/Signal/Inquire lines 464-518.
findings.required_fix: Add the two dilemma definitions and default/ordering details; optionally list beta parameter choices. Preserve the note’s caveat that source choice/initialization statements conflict.
findings.finding: The note still omits the formal sign-based rules that set the social and non-social dilemma flags, the default-zero values for non-choice alter information, and contact-history/next-alter ordering. These affect when and with whom exchanges occur. The two source conflicts (aspiration range and habit-choice condition) are now explicitly recorded accurately.

references.bibliography_scope: Captured reference-array integrity only; this focused audit did not reconcile HUMAT aliases against its full publisher bibliography.

notes.post_update_recheck: Current note checked after root edits. Both conflicts are now stated with accurate paired source descriptions; the previous source-conflict-unreported finding is resolved. Remaining FAIL finding concerns incomplete procedural mechanics.

notes.path: vault/Literature/Papers/Entries/How Does Facebook Retain Segregated Friendship- An Agent-Based Model Approach.md
notes.source_access: Full author preprint https://arxiv.org/pdf/2109.08862; publisher metadata and complete 59-item reference list https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/08944393231213960.

checks.equations_and_state: The corrected note properly distinguishes weighted Manhattan social-identity distance from eligibility; in this one-identity design w=1 and binary SI gives distance 0 or 1 (author PDF pp. 4-5, Eq. 1). The friendship rule is accurate: w_dist <= min(TOx, TOy), num_fx < TCx and num_fy < TCy (Eq. 2, pp. 5-6). Note could explicitly state the paper sets required tie length LT equal to w_dist for homogeneous/heterogeneous dyads (pp. 5-6, Fig. 2), but its inequality is equivalent for eligibility.
checks.update_and_partner_selection: Note accurately reports a stochastic initiator/target order, mandatory acceptance when both parties meet eligibility/capacity constraints, and stopping when no more ties can form (Simulation Procedure, pp. 8-9). The article does not provide a probability distribution or further partner-ranking rule; the note appropriately flags this limit.
checks.parameters_and_conflict: Correctly reports p=.22, w=1, n=30/300, TC means 3/30 and variance .25, TO Bernoulli(q), and 100 trials for each of six case-scenario cells (Simulation Design/Table 2, pp. 7-9). The unresolved q mismatch is correctly surfaced: Methods/Table 2 use {.2,.5,.8} (pp. 7-9); results narrative reports {.2,.5,.9} and 2.03%, 10.75%, 23.47% heterogeneous-dyad shares (pp. 12-13); p. 12 narrative says strongest segregation at q=.3; Table 3 uses .2/.5/.8 and Table 4 starts with .3, then .5/.8 (pp. 14-15). The note records methods/results/Table 4 values but omits the p. 12 q=.3 strongest-segregation statement. Its core warning that source values conflict is correct.
checks.results: Qualitative direction is supported: majority of dyads remain homogeneous; higher reported TO increases heterogeneous dyads; Facebook/offline-scale scenario combinations increase total ties while homogeneous share stays relatively stable; simulated individual same-ethnicity shares resemble empirical Hofstra benchmarks; Facebook-scale scenarios have all agents above the half-capacity satisfaction threshold (Results, pp. 12-16). The note omits useful numeric outcomes and should make explicit that population size n and capacity TC change together between offline and Facebook settings, preventing attribution of their separate effects. Its broad results statement is otherwise supported.
checks.metadata_and_bibliography: Publisher title, sole author, DOI and first-online date 2023-11-22 match SAGE metadata. All 59 current reference links were counted and their displayed-title sequence matches the 59 publisher References entries in order (publisher page lines 40-340); obsolete JSON body link excluded. The note’s footnote still describes alias reconciliation as pending, but this audit now confirms the 59-title publisher sequence.

findings.evidence: Author PDF Results pp. 12-15 reports heterophilous-dyad shares, ego-alter similarity percentages and empirical ratios; Simulation Design pp. 7-9 changes n and TC jointly.
findings.required_fix: Optionally include the main numeric outcome values, note that n and TC move together, and record the q=.3 strongest-segregation statement alongside the already reported parameter conflict.

findings.evidence: Author PDF pp. 5-6 says social identity distance determines required tie length and illustrates LT=w_dist; Eq. 2 uses w_dist <= min(TOx,TOy).
findings.required_fix: Optionally state explicitly that required tie length LT equals w_dist in this model application, while w_dist is still used as the eligibility quantity in Eq. 2.
